In Chin. and Eur. (see p.vii). Ph. Eur. 6.2 (Sodium Glycerophosphate, Hydrated). A white or almost white, crystalline powder or crystals. Freely soluble in water; practically insoluble in alcohol and in acetate. Profile Glycerophosphoric acid and various glycerophosphates have been used in tonics. They were once considered as a suitable means of providing phosphorus. Calcium and magnesium glyc- erophosphates (see p.1676 and p.1679, respectively) may be considered as a source of calcium or magnesium. ◊ Reference to the use of sodium glycerophosphate as a source of phosphorus in infant parenteral nutrition.1 1.
